newsitem.title: GREECE: Juppe urges Greece, Turkey to ease tensions.
newsitem.headline: Juppe urges Greece, Turkey to ease tensions.

text.p: Visiting French Prime Minister Alain Juppe urged Greece and Turkey on Saturday to avoid unilateral moves that could lead to a crisis in the region.
"There must be respect for international law and avoidance of unilateral actions that lead to problems and conflicts," he told reporters.
"Differences, when they exist, must be dealt with by international bodies, specifically the International Court at the Hague," he added.

Juppe, who is one a two-day visit to Greece to attend celebrations for the 150th anniversary of the French School in Athens, met Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis and Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos.
The two premiers told a joint news conference that they discussed European Union issues, bilateral relations and regional problems, including the divided island of Cyprus.
Cyprus is among several contentious issue between NATO members Greece and Turkey, who came close to war in January over a deserted islet in the eastern Aegean.
"We must avoid resorting to any violent solution, which always leads to escalation and tension," Juppe said. "There must always be dialogue and consultation with each other."
Juppe returns to Paris on Sunday night.
